body: `custom_draw_mode` stuff seems to be completely unrelated to `click`, should be a separate PR.
Okay, I'll move this to a separate PR. It was just the next logical step: the ability to change a button's appearance when it's programmatically clicked.

All of this padding is unrelated to the current PR. There's many exposed classes that don't pad all of the `bind_method` calls with new lines, either, so I would personally move it to a specialized PR.

diff_hunk:
@@ -22,6 +22,13 @@
 				Called when the button is toggled (only if [member toggle_mode] is active).
 			</description>
 		</method>
+		<method name="click">
+			<return type="void" />
+			<description>
+				Programmatically clicks the button, i.e. causes the corresponding virtual method to be called and the corresponding signal to be emitted, depending on [member toggle_mode]. If [member disabled] is [code]true[/code], nothing happens.
body:
```suggestion
				Presses the button. This causes the corresponding virtual method to be called and the corresponding signal to be emitted, depending on [member toggle_mode]. If [member disabled] is [code]true[/code], nothing happens.
```

In my opinion, such small code style improvements are appropriate to make along the way if you're touching the code. Of course, the scope of the stylistic improvements shouldn't significantly outweigh the useful changes.

I don't know if there's a general consensus on the blank lines in `_bind_methods()`, but here I encountered a situation where they're used for 3 setter/getter pairs, but not for the rest. The style is already mixed locally, and our only choice is to fix it here and now, or never. Because I have no desire to create a controversial large PR to enforce a uniform style globally and I don't think a separate PR to fix the empty lines within `BaseButton` deserves to exist.

This is pretty much the exact copy of `BaseButton::_accessibility_action_click` (callback for screen reader, which is not directly exposed), so its code can be deduplicated (changed to `press();` call).
